current_answer: Current evidence supports five distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end VSA queue-and-playout route; FastVideo FastH3 Preview has local clip paths; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining an unattended dense FastH3 channel at 22.1 fps through 448×448 output, prequeued prompts, and retimed playout; and Comfy’s optimized H3 path broadens local access. The consumer-channel report is not independent proof of 24-fps native motion, viewer-controlled interaction, cross-clip story continuity, uptime, or cost.

catalogue_card.question: Can one RTX 5090 keep FastH3 on air?
catalogue_card.text: A community project says yes at 22.1 fps, but only as a 448×448, prequeued, retimed channel of self-contained scenes—not a proven interactive 24-fps feed.

summary: A community FastH3 project reports a one-RTX-5090 ComfyUI channel at 22.1 sustained fps in its current dataset-card release. This is a self-reported one-machine result, not a pool test.

The route works as an unattended local channel because it prequeues work, uses self-contained scene prompts, retimes delivery, and accepts a 448×448 canvas. It does not establish native-24-fps motion or live viewer control.
FastVideo’s own example distinguishes VSA and dense FastH3 paths by adapter payload, so a timing without the checkpoint and attention path is not a portable FastH3 result.
Reactor’s four- and eight-B200 queue profiles and fal’s hosted Director session remain separate routes with different hardware, control, and continuity contracts.
uncertainty: The one-RTX-5090 FastH3 channel is a community project’s one-machine self-report; the pool has not run or independently audited it, and its downloadable files are access-gated.
Reactor’s playout, continuity, and four- or eight-B200 timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 15 September 2026. The one-RTX-5090 channel is a community self-report whose throughput, image quality, dependencies, licensing conditions, and long-run behavior need independent replication; FastH3 variants and local workflow settings move quickly.
